newsitem.title: FRANCE: Good beet conditions seen helping French yields.
newsitem.headline: Good beet conditions seen helping French yields.

text.p: Steady rain over the last two weeks has sharply improved growing conditions for sugar beets in France and farmers now see a chance for higher beet and sugar yields for the 1997/98 harvest.
"The crop potential is excellent. Beets are getting just the right combination of mild weather and rain," an analyst for the national sugar beet planters federation CGB told Reuters.
"At this stage we see a beet yield potential of 70 tonnes per hectare," he added. This would compare with a final beet yield of 66 tonnes per hectare achieved last year.
Asked about prospects for the 1997/98 sugar yield, he said, "We reached 10 tonnes per hectare last year. If good conditions persist, we could exceed that."
Dry conditions up to April 25 had slowed beet development but substantial rain in May helped make up for the delay.
Farmers again worried about a new bout of dry weather in early June. But scattered showers since mid-June helped speed up beet growth, which is now one week ahead of an average year.
Despite dry weather in March and April the number of beets per hectare was expected to be 100,000-110,000, in line with an average year, the analyst said.
The latest statistics from sugar and beet producers suggest area sown to sugar beets might decline by a marginal 0.25 percent from 422,000 hectares sown last year, he added.
France produced 4.226 million tonnes of beet sugar last year. --Dominique Vidalon, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
